static_findings.snippet: Stop writing `if (x !== null && x !== undefined)` everywhere.
- `O.flatMap(fn)` = "if we have something, apply this function"
- `O.getOrElse(() => default)` = "unwrap, or use this default if nothing"
**Plain language:** `flatMap` means "if this succeeded, try the next thing"
| Default for missing | "Use this if nothing" | `O.getOrElse(() => default)` |
| Transform if present | "If something, change it" | `O.map(fn)` |
| Chain nullable operations | "If something, try this" | `O.flatMap(fn)` |
| Wrap throwing function | "Try this, catch errors" | `E.tryCatch(fn, onError)` |
| Handle both cases | "Do this for error, that for success" | `E.fold(onLeft, onRight)` |

content.value_statement: TypeScript error and null handling often becomes repetitive or unclear. This skill applies practical fp-ts patterns with readable examples and restrained functional design.
actual_capabilities: Explains pipe, Option, Either, map, and flatMap with practical TypeScript examples.
Refactors nullable values, thrown errors, nested callbacks, and promise workflows into explicit functional patterns.
Compares imperative and fp-ts approaches to identify the clearer implementation.
Demonstrates typed error models, validation flows, and asynchronous failure handling.
Provides quick-reference guidance for common fp-ts operations and use cases.
limitations: Covers practical fp-ts fundamentals, not category theory or advanced functional programming.
Examples require adaptation to project types, fp-ts versions, and local conventions.
Does not execute code, install dependencies, or validate runtime behavior.
Does not replace tests, performance measurements, or team review.

use_cases.title: Learn Practical fp-ts
use_cases.description: Understand core fp-ts types through direct explanations and focused TypeScript examples.
use_cases.target_user: TypeScript developers new to functional programming

use_cases.title: Refactor Error Handling
use_cases.description: Replace exceptions, null checks, and nested callbacks with explicit, typed workflows.

use_cases.title: Review Functional Design
use_cases.description: Compare implementation options and keep functional patterns readable for the whole team.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Core Type
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how fp-ts Option handles nullable values, then show when native optional chaining is clearer.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Function
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this TypeScript function with Either, preserve its behavior, and explain each transformation in direct language: [function].

prompt_templates.title: Design an Async Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Model this asynchronous TypeScript workflow with TaskEither, typed failures, and readable pipe steps: [workflow requirements].

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate an fp-ts Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this fp-ts design for readability, error types, unnecessary abstraction, and team maintainability: [design or code].

output_examples.input: A function repeats null checks while reading a customer address. Recommend a practical approach.
output: Use optional chaining when the function only reads one short property path.
Use Option when several nullable operations must compose with later transformations.
Choose the approach that keeps missing-value behavior visible without adding unnecessary structure.

output_examples.input: Review a parser that throws exceptions for expected invalid input.
output: Return Either so callers can see success and failure in the type.
Define a focused validation error instead of returning unrelated strings.
Chain dependent validation steps with flatMap and transform successful values with map.

output_examples.input: Assess whether a data transformation pipeline uses too much functional abstraction.
output: Keep pipe when the transformations follow a clear reading order.
Replace indirect property helpers with direct callbacks when they improve recognition.
Use an imperative loop for measured hot paths or complex early exits.

best_practices: Introduce one fp-ts pattern at a time and preserve existing behavior.
Use explicit domain error types for expected failures.
Prefer the simplest approach that remains readable to the team.
anti_patterns: Do not replace short optional chains with long Option pipelines.
Do not hide simple transformations behind dense helper composition.
Do not adopt fp-ts without tests for success and failure paths.

faq.question: Does this skill require functional programming experience?
faq.answer: No. It explains core fp-ts patterns in direct language for TypeScript developers.

faq.question: Which fp-ts types does it cover?
faq.answer: It focuses on Option, Either, TaskEither, pipe, map, and flatMap.

faq.question: Can it refactor existing TypeScript?
faq.answer: Yes. It can propose focused refactors for nullable values, expected errors, validation, and asynchronous workflows.

faq.question: Will it always recommend fp-ts?
faq.answer: No. It recommends native TypeScript or imperative code when that approach is clearer.

faq.question: Does it test generated implementations?
faq.answer: No. You must run project tests, type checks, and performance measurements in your environment.

faq.question: Can it cover advanced functional abstractions?
faq.answer: Only at an introductory level. Its main scope is practical patterns used in common TypeScript applications.
